gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the big power stations use a lot of power just to keep their inverters running, which cuts into a 150 W pellet stove's runtime. The Solar Lab measured about 45 W idle on the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra and about 58 W on the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus. Best Batteries measured the Anker SOLIX F3800 delivering only about 65 % of its energy at a 200 W load. So the flat 85 % efficiency ChatGPT assumed is too high for these units at stove-sized loads.
standout_why: Solar Waypoint (cited) lists only maker specs (capacity, inverter watts, transfer time) and has no measured efficiency or idle draw. RuntimeMath (rank 1 in chat 2) applies a flat 0.85 factor to every unit, and its only own-draw figure is a maker-listed 20 W for the Apex 300. Best Batteries' Apex 300 review (rank 9 in chat 1, not cited) has measurements for the Apex 300 only (about 20 W idle, 2,290 Wh at 120 V), so rivals have part of this for the Apex 300 alone. Nothing ChatGPT got gives measured idle draw or low-load efficiency for the DELTA Pro Ultra, Jackery 5000 Plus, F3800 or DELTA Pro 3. I could not open the two cited Enough Watts pages (WebFetch hit a certificate error and curl was not allowed), so I have not checked them for this.
decides: The DELTA Pro Ultra still wins on total runtime. But its roughly 45 W idle draw adds about 30 % on top of a 150 W stove's draw, so ChatGPT's 35 h estimate is high. My rough estimate is closer to 30 h: 6,144 Wh × 0.95 ÷ (150 + 45) W, which is arithmetic, not a measurement. The ranking in the 4 kWh class changes. OutdoorGearLab measured 3,790 Wh from the DELTA Pro 3 (about 25 h at 150 W). The F3800's measured 65 % efficiency at 200 W leaves about 2,500 Wh (about 16.6 h at 150 W), not the 21.8 h ChatGPT showed. The 3,840 Wh F3800 therefore lasts less long on a stove than the DELTA Pro 3, and only slightly longer than the 2,765 Wh Apex 300 (2,290 Wh measured, about 15.3 h).
